title: USWNT’s Emma Hayes says Paul Green’s dedication to Chelsea was ‘unrivaled’
content:
U.S. women’s national team head coach Emma Hayes says her former Chelsea Women colleague Paul Green’s dedication to the club was “unrivaled”.

Chelsea announced on Feb. 9 that the club had parted ways with Green, who was a key component in establishing the London club’s dynasty during the 2010s and 2020s. Hayes and Green joined forces in 2013 and helped Chelsea win 15 trophies together, including a domestic treble in 2021 and five consecutive Women’s Super League (WSL) titles from 2020-2024.

“Paul was my partner in crime, he really was,” Hayes reflected Tuesday in a press conference, likening their partnership to that of Batman (or Batwoman in her case, she said) and Robin.

“Him and I were a perfect team. From the very first time I met him, coming from Doncaster Bells, he’d done every position in a football club. Side by side, we built Chelsea to be the club that they are, and he put so much into that, like, I think he virtually lived at the office.”

That office was at one point a curry house in Cobham (the town in England where Chelsea is based), Hayes joked. Working so close to an Indian restaurant helped her develop a taste for that cuisine, and she remembered fondly how much time she and Green spent at that curry house planning “all the little gains that it would take to go to the next level” with the club.

“He was completely dedicated to Chelsea, and what he did there at that club was unbelievable, I think unrivaled,” Hayes said.

“I think winning successive titles like we did, it’s so easy for everybody on the outside to say, ‘Oh, it’s because you had this, because I had that.’ Listen, at the heart of it was team, and at the heart of everything Paul displayed was the importance of those values alongside what it means to put that at the front of everything. I’m sure he will go on to great things, whatever he chooses to do, and I’m just so grateful I had the honor to work with him, truly.”

Green’s departure came at the tail end of a stretch of poor form from reigning league champions Chelsea, who sit third in the WSL table. They are nine points behind leaders Manchester City, to whom they suffered a devastating 5-1 defeat on Feb. 1 that raised pointed questions about the future of Chelsea manager Sonia Bompastor.

Five days later, though, Bompastor agreed to a contract extension with Chelsea that will run until 2030. Green was not quoted or mentioned in Chelsea’s announcement, while Bompastor confirmed last week that Chelsea will not replace the Englishman.

In reporting on Chelsea’s crisis, The Athletic spoke to several sources who, like Hayes, named Green as an integral component of the club’s success on the women’s side. Many of those sources also expressed a noticeable shift among Chelsea’s top brass, however, in which leadership once firmly concerned with the men’s side has been attempting to exert more authority over the women’s team. This, the sources added, has resulted in tensions around recruitment, efficient business transactions and long-term planning — responsibilities that historically fell under Green’s purview.

As it stands, several key Chelsea players’ contracts are set to expire this summer. Notably among them is USWNT striker Catarina Macario, who is working through an injury, along with center-back and captain Millie Bright, goalkeepers Hannah Hampton and Rebecca Spencer, strikers Sam Kerr and Aggie Beever-Jones, full-back Lucy Bronze, and winger Guro Reiten.
